title: SoftBank Surges as Asia Tech Stocks Rally on Wall Street AI Euphoria
excerpt: Japan's most valuable company leads a broad regional tech rally after the S&P 500 hit a record high, driven by blockbuster AI earnings and Middle East peace deal hopes.
body:
• SoftBank Group shares surged in Tokyo trading as Asian tech stocks tracked Wall Street's record-setting session, with the S&P 500 closing at an all-time high of 7,737 on August 4.
  • The Nikkei climbed 3.0%, South Korea's Kospi added 4.1%, and MSCI's broadest Asia-Pacific index rose 2.4% as semiconductor and AI-linked stocks led gains across the region.
  • Strong earnings from Palantir (93% revenue growth), Amazon, and Microsoft reinforced confidence that AI spending is accelerating, not peaking.
  • Falling oil prices on Middle East peace deal hopes provided additional tailwinds, with Brent crude dropping to $79.36 per barrel.

Wall Street Sets the Stage

Asian technology stocks rallied sharply on Wednesday as investors chased the momentum from a record-setting session on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 closed at an all-time high for the first time in two months.

SoftBank Group, now Japan's most valuable company with a market capitalization of roughly $290 billion, led the charge in Tokyo. The stock has become one of the clearest public-market proxies for the global AI boom, thanks to its approximately 90% stake in chip designer Arm Holdings and a roughly 13% stake in OpenAI worth an estimated $64.6 billion in committed investment.

The S&P 500 surged 1.8% on Tuesday to close at 7,737 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average broke above 54,000 for the first time, according to Reuters. The Nasdaq Composite gained 2.6%, marking its fourth consecutive day of more than 1% gains — a first in over a year.

AI Earnings Fuel the Fire

The rally was sparked by a wave of AI-linked earnings that reassured investors about the viability of massive data-center investments. Palantir reported 93% revenue growth in the latest quarter and raised its full-year revenue guidance by $500 million, according to Barron's. Caterpillar disclosed that power-generation sales to data-center operators jumped 48% during the quarter.

Earlier results from Amazon and Microsoft had already set an optimistic tone. Amazon reported accelerating growth in its cloud-computing business alongside heavy data-center investment, while Microsoft delivered blockbuster cloud revenue growth, according to the Wall Street Journal.

"Stronger results from a leading e-commerce and cloud service provider reinforced the view that AI-related capital expenditure continues to generate robust demand and attractive returns."

— Commerzbank Research

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index shot up nearly 7% on Tuesday, rising for a fourth straight session after tumbling 20.6% in July, Reuters reported. The rebound marked a sharp reversal from the summer selloff that had rattled chip-heavy markets across Asia.

Asia Catches the Wave

The momentum carried across the Pacific on Wednesday. Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 3.0%, South Korea's Kospi added 4.1%, and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 2.4%, according to Reuters. Chinese blue chips gained 0.7%.

SoftBank's rally extended a pattern that has defined 2026 for the stock. The company has surged roughly 73% year-to-date, overtaking Toyota to become Japan's largest listed company by market value. Its shares have repeatedly posted double-digit single-day gains during AI-driven rallies — jumping 18.4% in May on chip optimism and 13% in June after the Nikkei hit record highs, according to the Wall Street Journal and multiple market reports.

Across Asia, chip-related names surged. In South Korea, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics extended their runs as memory-chip leaders. In Taiwan, TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, added to recent gains. Samsung and SK Hynix each crossed $1 trillion in market value earlier this year, underscoring the scale of Asia's semiconductor-driven rally.

Middle East De-escalation Adds Tailwind

Easing geopolitical tensions provided an additional catalyst. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a deal to open the Strait of Hormuz could come within days, according to CNN. Qatar's foreign ministry described ongoing mediation efforts as being in "very progressive stages."

Brent crude fell to $79.36 per barrel on Tuesday — its lowest level since July 10 — after touching $102 in July. The drop in oil prices eased inflation fears and pushed bond yields lower, with 10-year Treasury yields falling to 4.603% from last week's high of 4.747%, Reuters reported.

What It Means for Indian Investors

The Asia tech rally has direct implications for Indian investors with exposure to global markets. SoftBank's portfolio includes significant Indian investments, and the broader AI-driven semiconductor cycle continues to benefit Indian IT services firms positioned in the AI infrastructure supply chain. India's own push into semiconductor manufacturing — with government-backed fab projects under construction — ties the country's industrial ambitions to the same capital-spending wave now lifting Asian tech stocks.

What's Next

The sustainability of the rally faces several tests. AMD fell 8.8% in after-hours trading despite beating earnings estimates, a reminder that investor expectations remain sky-high, according to Reuters. SpaceX shed 7.5% after hours on concerns about capital expenditure consuming cash flow.

"Because positioning and sentiment are a lot cleaner after the reset and rotation of the last eight weeks, the bull market has a much smoother path to capitalize on the earnings tailwind, which is larger than most estimated," Ross Mayfield, Baird investment strategist, told Barron's.

Friday's U.S. payrolls report will provide the next major market catalyst, with implications for Federal Reserve policy and the trajectory of bond yields that have constrained risk appetite for much of the summer.
nri_angle: SoftBank's portfolio includes significant Indian investments, and the AI-driven semiconductor cycle benefits Indian IT services firms and India's government-backed chip manufacturing push.
